2-Chloro-5-ethyl-6-methylpyridine-3-
carbonitrile 4a
A solution of 3a (48.7 g, 0.3 mol), phosphorus penta-
chloride (68.7 g, 0.33 mol) in phosphorus oxychloride
(200 mL) was heated to 80°C for 4 h. Phosphorus
oxychloride was evaporated under reduced pressure. The
resulting oil was poured cautiously into ice-water and the
semi-solid was extracted with chloroform (3xI00 mL).
The organic extract was washed successivelywith saturat-
ed aqueous sodium hydrogenocarbonate, water and brine.
The organic layer was dried over magnesium sulphate and
concentrated under reduced pressure to yield 40.5 g (75%)
ofa pale yellow solid: m.p. MOC; IR (KEr) 2220 (CN); -n
NMR (CDCI3) 8 (p.p.m.) 1.27 (t,] 7.3 Hz, 3H, CH3) ,
2.59 (s, 3H, CH3), 2.67 (q,]7.3 Hz, 2H, CHz), 7.73 (s,
IH, H4).

5-Ethyl-2-methoxy-6-methylpyridine-3-
carboxaldehyde 6a
A 1 M solution of diisobutylaluminium hydride (Dibal-
H) in tetrahydrofuran (THF) (120 mL, 0.12 mol) under
an argon atmosphere was cooled to O°C. A solution of 5a
(17.6 g, 0.1 mol) in anhydrous THF (50 mL) was added
over a period of 15 min. The reaction mixture was stirred
at room temperature overnight. The solvent was evaporat-
ed under reduced pressure and the resulting oil was cau-
tiously poured into
a mixture of ice-cooled 1 M
hydrochloric acid (150 mL) and diethylether (200 mL).
After 1 h the organic layer was
separated, washed with
